title: Saving for a First Home Takes Much Longer Now
summary:
Buying a first home has gotten much harder for many families in the United States, a new report says.

The Center for Responsible Lending studied how long renters need to save money to buy a small starter home. Buyers must pay a first chunk of money, called a down payment, plus extra fees.

The group found that a typical renter family now needs about 16 years to save enough. That is twice as long as in 2019. Teachers, nurses, firefighters and police officers need about 10 to 13 years.

Why? Homes cost more. Food, gas and rent cost more too. But many families' pay has not gone up as fast.

The wait is different in each city. It is 11 years in Houston and 24 years in Los Angeles.

The group wants more help for first-time buyers and more small, cheaper homes. Still, many young adults say they hope to own a home one day.
why_it_matters: Where your family can afford to live affects your home, school and neighborhood.
